basis: Read-only server probe of mcp.servers config (values only, credentials absent), repo Dockerfile.google/github-readonly.json, BUILD_LOG Phase 6 entries, and the Phase 11 product catalog in agentai_platform/connectors.py. No account was connected or read.
decision: All four account connectors and credentialed browsing are 'later' release scope per the requirement ledger (INT-01..05): OPTIONAL for private-beta launch, so their absence does not block launch; whatever is enabled must pass its gate. Brave search is live for the owner runtime only.

google-readonly.hardening: read-only rootfs, cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, 128 pids, 384m, user 1000, local files disabled, 5MiB file cap
google-readonly.caveat: One server serves Gmail, Calendar and Drive, so service separation depends on the OAuth scopes granted, not on process isolation. Its target email is an owner-provided config value, not verified identity.

github-readonly.caveat: Repository scoping comes from the credential's repository selection, which is unverified for this endpoint; per-customer GitHub App installation scoped to selected repos is the intended model and is unprobed.

brave-search.scope: OWNER RUNTIME ONLY. The single owner API key must never be shared into a customer cell; customer search needs a per-account metered route and call-fee attribution (Phase 5 gap), so it is off for customers.

gmail.token_storage: custody reference only (account-bound); never in DB/model/memory
gmail.revocation: disconnect deletes custody, cancels queued ops; provider-side revoke on rejected grants
gmail.billing: provider API quota only; no per-call fee known

calendar.read: today's events in the customer's timezone

drive.disclosure: drive.readonly can read every Drive file; prefer drive.file (items picked by the customer). A selection is mandatory either way and enforced server-side.

credentialed_browser.model: per-account profile (allowed hosts, credential_ref, session_ref in custody)
credentialed_browser.read: navigation only inside allowlisted HTTPS hosts; SSRF guard rechecked at every redirect
credentialed_browser.token_storage: encrypted custody; cookie jars are credential-bearing, so profile backups are encrypted with separately held keys
credentialed_browser.revocation: profile revoke deletes credential and session references
credentialed_browser.status: built, no login flow or custody backend, disconnected

provider_writes: Absent. The production catalog lists no writable kind for any service; a scope name is never approval. Enabling any write requires exact payload/target/expiry authorization (machinery built and tested with a synthetic service) AND native enforcement proof, which does not exist.
